reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) only generally states that Cr coatings peel/crack in high-temperature steam and that Al or Si must be considered in ATF cladding design. It provides no specific support for the key premises about alumina's diffusivity as a barrier, the graded interlayer's adhesion/thermal-mismatch benefits, ALD deposition of a ~20 nm alumina layer, or the predicted performance under the specified conditions.
premises: Cr coatings on Zr alloys suffer from interdiffusion and cracking/peeling in high-temperature steam
Alumina (Al2O3) has low atomic diffusivity and can block Cr–Zr interdiffusion
A graded interlayer can improve adhesion and reduce thermal mismatch between Zr alloy and alumina
ALD can deposit a dense, conformal ultrathin (~20 nm) alumina barrier
The modified coating will maintain protection under both subcritical water (~320 °C) and high-temperature steam (~1200 °C)
